definition: Dichotomy means a division or contrast between two things that are presented as opposite or entirely different.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word dichotomy. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know dichotomy should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her philosophy essay examined the dichotomy between theory and practice, asking why elegant ideas so often stumble in the real world.
A difference is weaker — two things can differ mildly in one detail, without dichotomy's sense of a sharp, two-sided split.
Polarization is stronger — it means the two sides are actively being pushed toward hostile extremes, beyond dichotomy's simple statement that two opposed categories exist.

A split is any clear division into separate parts — a band splits, a party splits into factions, a road splits in three. A dichotomy is a specific kind of split: exactly two parts, presented as opposites, with everything sorted onto one side or the other. Splits can be messy and many-way; a dichotomy is always a clean two.

A contrast is a striking difference you notice when two things are set side by side — it displays the difference and stops there. A dichotomy goes further: it divides a whole territory into exactly two opposed categories, so that everything must fall on one side or the other.

Opposition is the state of two things being actively set against each other — rivals, forces, or arguments in conflict. A dichotomy merely classifies: it claims there are exactly two categories, without the two sides doing battle. Teams in a match are in opposition; 'theory versus practice' is a dichotomy.

Dichotomy means a division or contrast between two things that are presented as opposite or entirely different.
The award-winning story builds its entire plot on the dichotomy between the frantic pace of the city and the slow rhythms of the family farm.
Dichotomy fits because the story sets up exactly two ways of life — city and farm — and treats them as sharply opposed worlds, which is the two-part, contrast-driven division the word names.
Dichotomy belongs to essays, lectures, and analysis, and it always implies exactly two sharply opposed parts — not a range and not many categories.
Watch for the common phrase 'false dichotomy,' which criticizes an argument for pretending only two options exist when there are really more.
